identity: Pyroscope Ruby FFI continuous profiler with rbspy native backend

previous_release.identity_checked: metadata.gz: pyroscope 1.0.6, x86_64-linux; original platform gem, not a reconstruction

decisive_diff: lib/pyroscope.rb, Gemfile, README.md, LICENSE and extconf.rb are byte-identical.
1.0.7 adds seven Rust source/build files through the gemspec file list; 1.0.6 omitted them.
Gemfile.lock changes only pyroscope version and Bundler 4.0.9 to 4.0.10.
Native source paths identify rbspy 0.46.0 to 0.47.0; Pyroscope 2.0.3 and remoteprocess 0.5.2 remain the same.

The complete PermissionDenied sudo retry message exists identically in both native binaries. Both versions fire the old rule under the current ruleset, contradicting the queue earlier clean-scan premise.
execution_trace: Ruby configure forwards the operator server URL, credentials, sampling configuration, tags and headers to initialize_agent. Default server: http://localhost:4040.
initialize_agent calls std::process::id at 0x152884 and Sampler::new at 0x1528bf, then builds the Pyroscope agent and starts ffikit::run at 0x152fd0.
Sampler reads Ruby stack frames using remoteprocess and read-process-memory. copy_address calls imported process_vm_readv at 0x3a84bd and falls back to proc-memory file I/O.
MemoryCopyError::fmt at 0x231a30 dispatches PermissionDenied to a 171-byte slice at 0x9b4ca8 and Formatter::write_str at 0x231af5. This is an error message, not a command execution path.
The two init_array functions are Rust argv initialization and frame_dummy. The five exported FFI entry points match the packaged Ruby bindings.

Pyroscope 2.0.3 session.send encodes pprof/profile metadata in a push request, gzips it, and POSTs to the configured server with optional configured authentication and headers; ffikit Kill stops profiling.
Decoded facts were inspected: apparent Base64/XOR/hex results are binary noise, numeric tables, JSON diagnostics and OpenSSL format strings. No decoded executable stage was found.

correction.unsupported_claim: The old nonroot-to-sudo regex treated user-directed retry advice as a sudo relaunch.
correction.retained_attack_claim: Require a diagnostic announcing an attempt to restart/relaunch or escalate privileges with sudo. Preserve the original ELF scope, suspicious severity and RustDesk exclusion.
correction.consumer_audit: No exact-ID or ancestor-directory rule consumers found for the corrected sudo trait. Other rules in the leaf are unchanged.

outside_batch_control.sudo_evidence: main: getuid at 0x40182d; nonroot branch builds sudo -E plus argv[0]; execvp at 0x401972

correction.focused_checks: 48 presence/absence checks across 12 ELF controls, with severity assertions. Covers retry advice, advice containing restarting, announced attempts, mixed advice/attempt, real dynamic import versus export/text, gzip Encoder versus Decoder.
correction.derived_finding_loss: Cargo.toml also loses an engine-generated notable references-malicious-component finding after the enclosing gem loses its false suspicious marker. Its Cargo pyroscope reference incorrectly points at file 0, the enclosing Ruby gem with the same name. This is not independent malicious-dependency evidence. No YAML rule defines that derived finding.

limits: Deployment configuration is unavailable. The destination is configurable; no particular deployment or operator consent is invented.
Static inspection establishes the error formatter, profiler calls and library capabilities; runtime success and an independently reproducible native build were not tested.
Atomscan warns that its feature model is v18 while the engine expects v21. Both root probabilities remain below its suspicious threshold; the judgement follows the code and release diff.

The engine still associates the Cargo pyroscope dependency with the enclosing same-named Ruby gem. Correcting this cross-ecosystem reference binding is outside YAML scope; it emits no remaining malicious-dependency finding in the final scan.
